comments.author: graton
comments.story: A Low-Fare Loophole for International Travelers
comments.why: Good info on the five freedoms of aviation.
comments.text: The five freedoms of aviation are: 1) The right to fly over a foreign country without landing. 2) The right to refuel or carry out maintenance in a foreign country without embarking or disembarking passengers or cargo. 3) The right to fly from one's own country to another country. 4) The right to fly from another country to one's own. 5) The right to fly between two foreign countries on a flight originating or ending in one's own country. This video has a lot of good info on it: [VIDEO] And wikipedia page: [LINK]

comments.text: Norwegian is technically an EU airline because despite the name they're also headquartered in EU countries. comments.author: laverya
comments.story: Major airline faces backlash after using ghost flights to exploit legal loophole
comments.why: Relevant explanation of international and domestic flight rules.
comments.text: You can't legally sell domestic flights in a foreign country. (for these purposes, the EU is one country) This is true for Australia, for India, for the USA, for the EU - an airline like Delta can fly to Sydney from LA but not sell domestic flights from Sydney to Melbourne. (Or, for that matter, international flights between Sydney and Singapore) However, there is a catch! Airliners did not used to have quite the range they do today, and so the treaties allow things like refueling stops. And they (sometimes!) allow passengers to embark/disembark at those stops - but those passengers still have to be flying the international leg, or else it would be a domestic flight.
